reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger, so I'll check the refunds list first.
The refunds ledger matches Alpha's handoff exactly. Next I'll check the orders list to confirm the refunds reference real orders and that the amounts are consistent before computing payouts.
The refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff exactly, and each refund is within its order amount, so I found no problem. Next I'll get the net balance for each customer, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 40355 matches its order total with no refunds, so the ledger looks consistent. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Acme (40355) and birch (40935) both match their order totals minus refunds. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance before deciding whether anything needs a hold.

All three net balances match order totals minus the listed refunds: acme 40355, birch 51183−10248=40935, cobalt 37699−11984=25715. The refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff, so I found no reason to hold. I'll record acme's payout first.

Acme's payout of 40355 recorded successfully. The other two balances also check out: birch is 51183 minus 10248 = 40935, and cobalt is 37699 minus 11984 = 25715, with the refunds matching Alpha's handoff. No hold is needed, so I'll record birch's payout next.

Cobalt's balance of 25715 matches its orders (9909 + 27790 = 37699) minus the refunds for orders 292 and 295 (2929 + 9055 = 11984). Acme and birch already paid out, so I'll record cobalt's payout now.
All three payouts are recorded. Each amount matches its order total minus the refunds in the ledger, and the ledger matches Alpha's handoff.
